question: A new team member asks how the Claude model tiers actually differ from one another in everyday use. Which two statements are accurate? Select two.
options: A) The tiers differ only in writing style, so any of them may be used for any task at any time.
B) The deepest tier suits genuinely hard problems, and it consumes meaningfully more allowance.
C) Moving up one tier is the standard fix whenever a prompt comes back with a vague or shallow answer.
D) The mid tier is the fast, capable default, and it is the right pick for most everyday work.
E) The lightest tier gives answers of the very same depth, only more slowly than the other two.
correct_answers: B) The deepest tier suits genuinely hard problems, and it consumes meaningfully more allowance.
D) The mid tier is the fast, capable default, and it is the right pick for most everyday work.
explanations: Incorrect. The difference is reasoning depth, speed and cost, not writing style, and the tiers are not interchangeable.
Correct. The deepest tier buys reasoning depth for harder problems and costs meaningfully more of the usage allowance.
Incorrect. A vague answer usually signals an under-specified prompt, and a deeper tier cannot supply context that was never given.
Correct. The middle tier is positioned as the fast, capable default that handles most knowledge work well.
Incorrect. The lightest tier is the fastest of the three, and it trades some reasoning depth for that speed and low cost.
